column1: # landmines.tsv -- what this project already learned, keyed by what a DIFF touches.
# Read by tools/buildgate/precheck.sh before every build.  The problem it solves:
# the lessons were all written down (docs/, the memory notes) and were still not
# in mind at the moment of the decision.  So recall is not left to memory -- the
#   1  id        short name, used for the bench stamp
#   2  regex     extended regex, matched against the diff since the last PASSING
#                build: changed FILE PATHS and changed LINES (added and removed)
#   3  bench     command that must PASS before the build may start, or "-"
#   4  note      what was learned.  Name the memory note / doc so it can be opened.
# Add a line whenever a build, a board session or a day is lost to something a
# one-line warning would have prevented.  Keep the regex on the SMELL of the area
# (signal names, file names, idioms), not on one exact line.

column4: The hand-over COPIES one register context across; the BIOS overlay stub (single OUT (E5),A at 0180h) is its other half.  The real CHGCPU writes TWO bytes with OTIR ([mode,60h]) because real hardware has two independent CPUs parked mid-OTIR -- under the copy model the incoming core inherits PC=OTIR,B=1 and writes the 60h at once, bouncing back to Z80 in 0.7 us.  Removing the stub killed every R800 switch (20260922b).  memory: feedback-chestertons-fence-before-removing-rtl

column3: verilator --binary -Wno-fatal -Wno-WIDTH -Wno-DECLFILENAME -Wno-UNUSEDSIGNAL -Wno-UNDRIVEN --top-module tb -o tbevt -Mdir /tmp/buildgate_bench/evt tools/evtrace/tb_evt.sv rtl/evt_trace.sv >/dev/null 2>&1 && /tmp/buildgate_bench/evt/tbevt | grep -c MARKER | grep -qx 4
column4: A repeat COUNT cannot find a wedge, only time can: LDIR looks like jr $, and the turbo R BIOS RAM search repeats one address 28672 times while working.  CALL 0038 is NORMAL in Illusion City's ISR -- an 0038 fetch without INTA is not by itself a runaway.  tools/evtrace/README.md

ch2 has no handshake at stock speed (open-loop deadline) and a hit LEVEL plus a done TOGGLE when paced.  Stale reads have cost this project twice: the vgmplay freeze, and 20260922 a stack read that returned the previous opcode byte (F392 read as F3C9) in the 21 MHz window right after a CPU hand-over.  memory: project-vgmplay-freeze-rootcause, project-sdram-readcache

A second `load` racing the FSM restart released the machine on half-written SDRAM (36 corrupt products in 300 trials before e23e531).  reset_rq is LOW before a load starts as well as after it.  STATE_CLEAN does not clear ref_ram/offset_ram.  docs/handoff_20260920_hangs.md

A write to 0FFFFh in an expanded slot must latch the subslot register and go nowhere else; unmapped reads are FFh and FFh executes as RST 38h, so a wrong decode looks like a runaway, not like a bus error.

MiSTer's menu silently ignores what it has not seen before: token index 1 is reserved (SS/UART/MIDI), an `I` token in the middle shifts every row below it, status bits above the highest precedent do nothing, and a "free" bit may hold a stale 1 in the user's MSX1.CFG -- read the board's CFG with xxd first.  memory: feedback-stay-inside-proven-range, reference-confstr-i-token-placement

Shared VDP timing signals have many consumers: enumerate them ALL before changing one, write the invariants both ways first, and verify on several games (they measure the IRQ period themselves).  A GND warning may be intent.  memory: feedback-vdp-timing-change-protocol

No division and no large combinational cloud inside the PCM engine: a signed /12 grew a LUT cloud that broke SDRAM_DQ IOB packing and made 2 MB RAM read 0/384KB at random -- silently, on the board only.  Re-verify 2 MB RAM after any change here.  memory: project-pcm-noise-rootcause, reference-pcm-engine-optimization
Gain and trim changes need the user's permission first; a label that does not match the real gain is a lie, and the user works from a level meter.  memory: feedback-gain-changes-need-permission

ghdl synth exits 0 with black-boxed entities when a package is analysed twice -- only the Verilator lint catches it.  spram/dpram stubs MUST return FFh when cs=0 or the runaway being hunted disappears from the simulation.  sim/fullsys/README.md

The turbo R disk ROM block (TURBOR_FDC) is a 64 kB DOS 2.30/2.31 kernel banked on a write to 7FF0 with the WD2793 registers at 7FF8-7FFF in the SAME page.  The bank window must be 7FF0 alone: with the generic MSXDOS2 windows a 6000-6FFF write (any ASCII8 probe) or 7FFE flips the kernel bank under the running driver.  The ROM itself is synthesized (tools/turbor_diskrom/synth2.py): 34 patches that re-link the hb-f1xd WD2793 driver into the ASCII kernel; every patch asserts the original byte.  docs/turbor_diskrom_20260923.md

The kanji post-read increment fires one clock AFTER ram_ce falls; on nz_bus (NextZ80) the next stage address is already on the bus there, so choosing addr1/addr2 from the live addr[1] bumped the JIS2 counter (R800 read the same JIS1 byte twice, a plain IN loop gave byte 0 forever -- board 2026-09-23, reproduced by sim/fullsys/tb_kanji.sv).  Any device that keys a post-cycle action on the address bus needs the select latched while the strobe is high.  make -C tb kanji runs both bus shapes.  See project_illusion_city / handoff_20260923_turbor §3.

The PCM engine has broken SILENTLY before (a signed /12 LUT wrecked IOB packing and 2MB RAM came back 0/384KB at random).  Never change it without the bit-exact golden run, and never trust that run without checking it BUILT what you changed: the runner used to swallow the compile error and re-run the previous binary, printing ALL SCENARIOS MATCH for code that does not compile (2026-09-24).  Verilator is the default simulator because iverilog cannot elaborate per-field writes into an unpacked array element.  memory: reference-pcm-engine-optimization, feedback-verify-the-build-contains-it.

A save/load request is a HOST command and must be latched OUTSIDE the reset branch.  `load_sram` is one clock wide and memory_upload raises it on the edge reset_rq falls, while MSX1.sv stretches the machine reset 63 clk21m past that -- so a latch inside `if (reset) ... else` threw it away and no .sav was read on a ROM load for four days, with the OSD SRAM Load still working because that path has no reset (20260920 8d1d8bf -> 20260924).  Widening a reset can break anything that samples a pulse.  memory: project-ascii16x-flash.

MSX-MIDI is mostly WIRING, not chip behaviour: status bit 7 is the 8251 DSR pin tied to the TIMER IRQ line (not a USART bit), DTR enables the timer IRQ and RTS enables the RxRDY IRQ, 8254 CLK0/CLK2 are 4 MHz and CLK1 is OUT2, and OUT0 is the baud clock.  The bench drives the FS-A1GT BIOS sequence measured on openMSX (PC 1A31-1A6B) and checks 500 kHz / 200 Hz / both interrupts / TX / RX / loopback.  Two bugs it caught: mode 3 reloading N/2 instead of N ran the port at twice the baud rate, and shifting on the start-bit edge sent every byte rotated.  memory: project-midi.

MSX1.sv is in NO bench: sim/fullsys simulates the machine and leaves the MiSTer wrapper out, so a wrong port on an instance there reaches Quartus and fails Analysis & Synthesis 25 minutes in.  `.dbg_wait_ratio(...)` exists on two instances and an edit meant for `msx MSX` landed on the debug overlay (20260924).  tools/lint_top.sh elaborates the real top in seconds.
